page: Amazon Web Services r7i.48xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 192 vCPUs and 96 physical cores based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. It does not include local storage or GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 169,761.83 and a Passmark CPU score of 123,948.44. The DDR5 memory subsystem delivers top-tier read-only large block bandwidth of 454.59 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth of 190.44 GB/sec. The processor's advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512, contribute to top-tier performance in extended instructions and encryption tests. In-memory database performance is highly competitive, with Redis SET operations reaching 183.87 million operations per second.

The server offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads, though the lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs. The absence of dedicated GPUs is partially mitigated by strong CPU-based LLM inference capabilities, achieving 41.22 tokens per second on 7B models. This hardware profile is highly cost-efficient for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise applications, software compilation, and data-intensive workloads that require substantial memory capacity alongside high-throughput multi-core processing.
